England primary maths · Year 4

Year 4 maths.
Stronger basics, one match at a time.

Every times table through 12 × 12. Four-digit columns, fractions and decimals. Area, angles, symmetry, coordinates and graphs. Use the academy alongside teaching and practical learning.

Build a Year 4 player

What does Year 4 practice focus on?

01

Every times table through 12 × 12

02

Four-digit columns, fractions and decimals

03

Area, angles, symmetry, coordinates and graphs

The map below names 57 practice families available for this year. Supporting skills can be revisited when a pupil needs them. Schools may sequence content differently within a key stage.

Roman numerals to 100

Patterns in multiplication

Written multiplication

Recall and connections

Times tables in Year 4

Consolidate all multiplication facts through 12 × 12 and related division. Keep reviewing facts while applying them in the wider curriculum.

Times-table guide

Beyond a number answer

A grown-up records practical and reasoning work alongside digital practice.

  • Measure perimeter and area
  • Construct a symmetric figure
  • Plot and translate a polygon
  • Present discrete and continuous data
  • Explain a method choice

How Year 4 promotion works

XP rewards effort and independent answers, but does not award a completed year. The academy checks broad independent coverage and later-day recall across this year’s families. Practical observations are recorded by a grown-up. A 12-shot promotion match then requires at least 90% independent accuracy, with the other goals still satisfied. Earlier facts remain available for review after promotion.

This is an in-game progression policy. It is not a DfE-approved pass mark, a diagnostic judgement or a guarantee that a skill will never be forgotten.
